title: Admin - Assign Admin Role - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin User & Role Management - Assign Admin Role feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Super Admins to assign or change roles (Super Admin, Limited-Access Admin) via an editable role dropdown on admin cards. Changing a role automatically updates permissions, and the change is saved instantly or on confirmation. Covers happy path, role switching, permission auto-update, edge cases (last Super Admin downgrade, backend error, refresh during update).

testCases.title: Role dropdown is visible and editable on admin cards
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. User & Roles page is loaded with at least one admin card.
steps: Locate the role indicator on the card
Verify the role can be changed (dropdown or editable control)
expectedResults: Each admin card displays the current role (Super Admin or Limited Access Admin)
The role is displayed as an editable dropdown or clickable control
Clicking/interacting with the role opens a selection with available options
The dropdown is not disabled or read-only

testCases.title: Role dropdown shows both available roles
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Role dropdown is open on an admin card.
steps: Click on the role dropdown for any admin
expectedResults: The dropdown shows exactly two options: 'Super Admin' and 'Limited-Access Admin'
Both options are selectable
The currently assigned role is indicated (highlighted or checked)
No other role options are present
testCases.postconditions: Both role options are visible in the dropdown

testCases.title: Change role from Limited-Access Admin to Super Admin
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. A Limited-Access Admin exists in the list.
steps: Click the role dropdown on that card
expectedResults: The role changes from 'Limited Access Admin' to 'Super Admin'
The change is saved (instantly or after confirmation)
The admin card now displays 'Super Admin' as the role
A success notification may be shown
The permissions section updates to show all permissions
testCases.postconditions: Admin role is changed to Super Admin with full permissions

testCases.title: Change role from Super Admin to Limited-Access Admin
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Multiple Super Admins exist (not the last one).
steps: Find a Super Admin card (not the last Super Admin)
Click the role dropdown on that card
expectedResults: The role changes from 'Super Admin' to 'Limited Access Admin'
The change is saved successfully
The admin card now displays 'Limited Access Admin' as the role
The permissions section updates (may show reduced permissions or prompt for permission selection)
testCases.postconditions: Admin role is changed to Limited-Access Admin

testCases.title: Changing role updates permissions automatically
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. A Limited-Access Admin with specific permissions exists.
steps: Find a Limited-Access Admin card with partial permissions (e.g., Dashboard, Partner Management)
Observe the permissions section on the card
expectedResults: After changing to Super Admin, all permissions are automatically assigned
The permissions section shows all available modules (Dashboard, User Management, Partner Management, Product Management, Comment Moderation, Content Management, Analytics)
The permission update happens automatically without manual selection
No user action is needed to assign permissions after role upgrade
testCases.postconditions: Permissions are automatically updated to match the new role

testCases.title: Permissions reduce when downgrading from Super Admin to Limited-Access
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. A Super Admin (not the last one) exists with all permissions.
steps: Find a Super Admin card (showing all 7 permissions)
expectedResults: After downgrading, permissions are adjusted (either reduced to a default set or cleared for re-assignment)
The admin card no longer shows all 7 permissions
The system either prompts for new permission selection or assigns a default subset
The change is reflected immediately on the card
testCases.postconditions: Permissions are adjusted after role downgrade

testCases.title: Role change is saved instantly or on confirmation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. An admin card is available for role change.
steps: Change an admin's role via the dropdown
Observe whether the change saves immediately or requires confirmation
expectedResults: The role change is either saved instantly (auto-save) OR a confirmation dialog appears
If instant: the card updates immediately and a success notification may appear
If confirmation: a dialog asks 'Are you sure?' with Confirm/Cancel options
After page refresh, the role change is still reflected (persisted to backend)
The change is not lost on refresh
testCases.postconditions: Role change is persisted to the backend

testCases.title: Cannot downgrade the last remaining Super Admin
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Only ONE Super Admin exists in the system (the current user or another).
steps: Identify the last remaining Super Admin
Attempt to change their role to 'Limited-Access Admin'
expectedResults: The system prevents the role change
An error message is displayed (e.g., 'Cannot downgrade the last Super Admin. At least one Super Admin must exist.')
The role dropdown reverts to 'Super Admin'
No change is saved to the backend
The admin retains their Super Admin role
testCases.postconditions: Last Super Admin cannot be downgraded — system enforces minimum one Super Admin

testCases.title: Role change fails due to backend error
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Backend API is configured to fail on role update (or network issue simulated).
steps: Attempt to change an admin's role
Observe the error handling when the API fails
expectedResults: An error notification is displayed (e.g., 'Failed to update role. Please try again.')
The role dropdown reverts to the original value (no inconsistent state)
The permissions do not change (remain as before the attempt)
The user can retry the action
No partial/corrupt state is saved
testCases.postconditions: Role reverts to original on backend failure

testCases.title: Page refresh during role update does not corrupt data
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. About to change an admin's role.
steps: Initiate a role change on an admin card
Immediately refresh the page (F5) before the save completes
Observe the admin's role after page reload
expectedResults: After refresh, the admin's role is in a consistent state
Either the old role is shown (change didn't complete) OR the new role is shown (change completed before refresh)
No corrupted/partial state exists
The permissions match the displayed role
No error messages appear on the refreshed page
testCases.postconditions: Data is consistent after refresh during update

testCases.title: Role change on one admin does not affect other admins
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Multiple admins exist in the list.
steps: Note the roles of all visible admins
Change the role of one specific admin
expectedResults: Only the targeted admin's role changes
All other admin cards retain their original roles
No unintended side effects on other admins
The admin count remains the same
testCases.postconditions: Role change is isolated to the targeted admin only

testCases.title: Selecting the same role (no change) does nothing
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. An admin with 'Super Admin' role exists.
steps: Select 'Super Admin' (the same role already assigned)
expectedResults: No change occurs — the role remains 'Super Admin'
No API call is made (or if made, it's a no-op)
No success/error notification is shown (or a neutral message)
Permissions remain unchanged
testCases.postconditions: No unnecessary update when same role is selected

testCases.title: Role change is reflected in the role filter results
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Role filter is available.
steps: Filter by 'Limited-Access Admin' and note the count
Change one Limited-Access Admin to 'Super Admin'
expectedResults: After the role change, the admin no longer appears in the 'Limited-Access Admin' filter
The Limited-Access Admin count decreases by 1
The admin now appears in the 'Super Admin' filter
The Super Admin count increases by 1
testCases.postconditions: Role change is correctly reflected in filter results

testCases.title: Confirmation dialog (if present) can be cancelled
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Role change triggers a confirmation dialog.
steps: Change an admin's role to trigger confirmation
expectedResults: The confirmation dialog closes
The role reverts to the original value
No change is saved to the backend
The admin card shows the original role and permissions
testCases.postconditions: Cancelling confirmation reverts the role change

testCases.title: Super Admin cannot change their own role to Limited-Access (self-downgrade prevention)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. The current user's admin card is visible in the list.
steps: Find the current user's own admin card
Attempt to change own role to 'Limited-Access Admin'
expectedResults: The system either prevents self-downgrade with an error message
OR the dropdown is disabled/hidden for the current user's own card
OR the system allows it but warns that the user will lose Super Admin access
The system ensures at least one Super Admin always exists
